newsitem.title: USA: Rock-Tenn sees drop in Q1 sales, income.
newsitem.headline: Rock-Tenn sees drop in Q1 sales, income.

text.p: Rock-Tenn Co said Wednesday it expects its fiscal first quarter net sales and net income to be "significantly" below year-ago results.
Rock-Tenn, which manufactures clay-coated and uncoated recycled paperboard, earned $11.8 million, or $0.35 a share, on net sales of $219.4 million in the fiscal 1996 first quarter.
The company cited continued pricing pressure and an earlier than expected seasonal slowdown in product shipments for the expected drop in results for the first quarter, ending December 31.
Rock-Tenn also said its November results reflected 11 percent lower sales compared to the same month in 1995.

"The December quarter usually reflects seasonal weakness in demand for converted products. Demand in the September quarter was stronger than we had anticipated and the seasonal slowdown appears to have begun in early November," said Jay Shuster, Rock-Tenn's president.
For the first two months of the December quarter, the average price for Rock-Tenn's recycled paperboard declined by about $80 per ton from the same quarter last year, the company said.
